target.title: perf(mapper): cache full-root filesystem scans across concurrent mappers
target.body:
## Description
This PR addresses a significant performance bottleneck during the initial feature mapping phase. Previously, the Go, C/C++, and Dotnet mappers unconditionally ran full-root walk() scans in parallel. In large polyglot monorepos, this resulted in 3x redundant disk I/O (redundant readdir and lstat syscalls) because these ecosystems support mapping loose source files without root-level configuration files.

## Changes Made
VFS Cache Module: Created src/mappers/vfs-cache.ts to memoize readdir, lstat, and realpath filesystem operations using Promises.
MapperContext Update: Injected the VFS cache into the orchestrator's MapperContext so it lives for the duration of a single mapFeatures run.
walk Helper: Updated the shared walk() function in shared.ts to optionally accept and use the VFS cache for all underlying I/O.
Mapper Integration: Updated go.ts, c-cpp.ts, and dotnet.ts to pass the context.vfs down to their full-root traversals.

## Impact
Concurrent mappers hitting the same directories now share the exact same I/O operation (the first mapper pays the disk cost, and subsequent mappers instantly receive the cached memory representation). This results in a ~66% reduction in filesystem syscalls during initialization. Language-specific filters (e.g., shouldSkipCOrCppPath) continue to function identically on the cached arrays.


### Real Behavior Proof & Regression Coverage
- **Error Semantics Repaired**: Removed the broad `readdir` fallback that was silencing directory-read failures. Added focused cache/error regression coverage in `vfs-cache.test.ts` to ensure `EACCES` and transient errors are preserved, memoized, and correctly bubbled up to the mappers.
- **Syscall Reduction**: By injecting the shared `MapperContext.vfs` into `walk()`, concurrent full-root scans now securely share `Promise` state in memory. In polyglot repos where `go list` fails (triggering Go's fallback walk), the C/C++, .NET, and Go mappers hit the disk exactly once per directory. Memory sharing eliminates the redundant `readdir` and `lstat` syscalls entirely for the trailing mappers.


- Fixes #158
